items.label: text
items.text: Be careful with the wording of your answer in the exam - the concentrations of the reactants and products at equilibrium are constant, they are not equal.

items.label: caption
items.text: Figure 21.4 The rates of the forward reaction and the reverse reaction become equal when equilibrium is reached.

items.label: text
items.text: Soon the rates of both reactions become equal. At that point, blue squares are changing into yellow ones at exactly the same rate that yellow ones are turning blue.

items.label: text
items.text: What would you see in the reaction mixture when that happens? The total numbers of blue squares and of yellow squares would remain constant, but the reaction would still be happening. If you followed the fate of any one particular square, sometimes it would be blue and sometimes yellow.

items.label: list_item
items.text: Figure 21.5 The reaction continues, but total numbers of blue and yellow squares remain constant.

items.label: text
items.text: This is an example of a dynamic equilibrium. It is dynamic in the sense that the reactions are still continuing, but the rate of the forward reaction is equal to the rate of the reverse reaction. It is an equilibrium in the sense that the total amounts or concentrations of the various things present (reactants and products) are now constant.

items.label: text
items.text: Notice that you can set up a dynamic equilibrium only if the system is closed in a sealed container. If, for example, you removed the yellow squares as soon as they were formed, they would never get the chance to turn blue again. What was a reversible reaction would now go entirely in one direction as blue squares turn yellow without being replaced.

items.label: text
items.text: Consider the reversible reaction that occurs when calcium carbonate decomposes:

items.label: formula
items.text: C a C O _ { 3 } ( s ) \rightleftharpoons C a O ( s ) + C O _ { 2 } ( g )

items.label: text
items.text: If this were not done in a closed container then all the CO2 would escape and the reverse reaction would not occur.

items.label: text
items.text: Reversible reactions will eventually reach a state of equilibrium if they are left in a sealed container.

items.label: text
items.text: Taking a general case where A reacts reversibly to give B:

items.label: text
items.text: The reaction from A to B (the left-to-right reaction)is described as the forward reaction. The reaction between from B to A (the right-to-left reaction)is called the reverse reaction.
